newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Injured Waller may miss 2 Super 12 games.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Injured Waller may miss 2 Super 12 games.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, April 22 - Wellington Hurricanes lock Dion Waller will miss next Saturday's Super 12 game against the Otago Highlanders and possibly the following one against New South Wales, NZPA reports.
Waller suffered a medial ligament strain to his right knee during the match against Free State on Sunday and has been told it may take 10 days to two weeks to recover.
The injury happened 26 minutes into the second half at Athletic Park on Sunday when he stepped over a player in a maul and a Free State player and a Hurricanes team-mate twisted him.
"I immediately thought the worst because I remember (Hurricanes team-mate) Chresten Davis doing his knee there last year," he said.
He can walk and has the knee strapped up but it is swollen and he is having physiotherapy.
"When you are playing so well I would rather stay on the field. I would like to be right for New South Wales (at Napier)."
The knee will be examined again when the Hurricanes assemble in Wellington on Wednesday.
Last year Waller was out of action for six weeks after injuring a knee cartilage and a shin with the Hurricanes in South Africa.
Waller was thrilled to play in front of the huge Wellington crowd on Saturday and like fellow lock Mark Cooksley, both from the Waikato Chiefs region, has few doubts he is in the right Super 12 side.
